subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Rocket Nozzles: Shaping the Exhaust
description: A short lesson to help you apply Rocket Nozzles: Shaping the Exhaust.

hook.text: A rocket nozzle doesn't just direct the exhaust. It accelerates gases from subsonic to supersonic speed. The shape is everything.

buildup.text: The de Laval nozzle first narrows to a throat, then widens. The narrow throat chokes the flow to exactly Mach 1.

discovery.text: After the throat, the expanding section accelerates gas beyond Mach 1. Counterintuitively, a wider path speeds up supersonic flow.

twist.text: Nozzle size must match altitude. A sea-level nozzle is too small for vacuum, and a vacuum nozzle separates flow at sea level.

climax.text: Aerospike nozzles adjust automatically to altitude. They perform well from sea level to vacuum but are mechanically complex.

punchline.text: Narrow, then wide. Subsonic to supersonic. The nozzle does the magic.

quiz.question: Why does a de Laval nozzle first narrow then widen?
options: The narrow section filters out combustion particles before they exit
The throat chokes flow to Mach 1, and the expanding section accelerates it to supersonic speed
The widening section cools the gas to prevent the nozzle from melting
